# Davidson Day School — International Travel — Deep Research (transcription)

> **⚠️ AI-GENERATED LEAD SHEET — NOT A PRIMARY SOURCE.** This is a transcription of a
> Claude deep-research PDF. Nothing in it may reach the app on its own authority. A fact
> renders only once it is confirmed on a live davidsonday.org page (or a Wayback copy of
> one) and recorded in `Davidson Day - International Travel - Source URLs.md`, which is the
> citation record.

 Programs — Research Dossier (as of October 2026)*
- Filename: `Davidson_Day_School_Global_Travel_and_Global_Studies_Programs__2026_Research_Dossier.pdf`
 (10 pages, created 2026-10-18)
- Produced by Claude deep research from the `/global-exposure` mode-A prompt
 (`.claude/skills/global-exposure/prompt-template.md`), run by the user 2026-10-18.
- Transcribed 2026-10-18 by `/global-exposure` mode B. The PDF's [Official]/[Secondary]

 found the PDF wrong or out of date.
- **No student is named in this file.** The PDF named none; several school posts it cites

 and never render (privacy rule).

Davidson Day's global program is built around two things: a Global Studies Diploma
Distinction for the Upper School, and summer international travel. Upper School travel
runs through AFAR, an archaeology nonprofit founded by the school's Director of Global
Studies, which digs in Spain, Portugal and Belize. Middle School has a summer
language-and-culture trip to Spain and France. The school's own website publishes very
little about eligibility rules, dates, prices, aid or participation. Most hard numbers
come from AFAR's site (goafar.org) and are [Secondary].

▶ The International Travel page (`/student-life/international-travel`) now returns **404**
and is gone from the site nav (checked twice, 2026-10-18). Its content survives in Wayback
copies of 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-07. The Middle School Spain/France section is in the
February copy and **absent from the March copy**.

sections.text:
- **What exists [Official]:** "Davidson Day offers summer international trips for our
 Middle and Upper School students" (https://www.davidsonday.org/student-life/international-travel).
 Upper School travel is the AFAR archaeology field program in "Spain, Portugal, and
 Belize". Middle School has "a summer language and cultural immersion trip to Spain and
 France". The credential is the Global Studies Diploma Distinction, which has "existed at
 Davidson Day School since 2021" (https://www.davidsonday.org/academics/diploma-distinctions/global-studies).
- **What is missing:** trip dates, prices, deposits, group sizes, selection, the Middle
 School vendor, safety/passport guidance, exchange partners and graduate counts are NOT
 PUBLISHED on the school site. No Round Square, sister-school or homestay program found.
- **The money [Secondary]:** AFAR lists 2026–27 fees of "$6850" (Spain), "$7750"
 (Portugal) and "$6779" (Belize), including round-trip airfare from Charlotte; AFAR offers
 a "maximum of 20% in assistance for the 2026 field season" (https://www.goafar.org/scholarships).
 The school's aid FAQ [Official] is silent on trips; it lists a "Field Experience (4th -
 12th Grade)" fee of "$500 - $1,000" (https://www.davidsonday.org/admission/tuition-and-affordability).
 No travel-specific endowment or named fund found.
- **Bottom line:** the archaeology research pathway is unusual and substantive (students
 present at a university conference; ten went to Calgary in 2024), but the program is
 narrow, depends on one person, and is thinly documented.

sections.text:
- **Names and branding [Official]:** page titled "International Travel", tagline "Beyond
 the Classroom. Around the World.", two parts: "Upper School International Travel and
 Research" and "Middle School International Travel". The credential is one of three
 Diploma Distinctions (with Business and Civic Engagement, and STEMM).
- **Mission [Official]:** "These trips invite students to explore new cultures, grow as
 global citizens, and step outside their comfort zones and into a broader understanding of
 the world and themselves." Credential: "The Global Studies Diploma Distinction prepares
 students to understand an increasingly interconnected world through rigorous academic
 study, language immersion, and transformative international experiences". Older page:
 "The Global Studies Diploma Program offers students the opportunity to develop a
 culturally diverse perspective, both through curricular and experiential learning."
- **AFAR [Official]:** "The American Foreign Academic Research (AFAR) Program at Davidson
 Day is pioneering full-scale international archaeological field research and cultural
 site preservation for pre-collegiate students in Spain, Portugal, and Belize."
- **Naming conflict [Official vs Official]:** the IT page says "American Foreign Academic
 Research"; the 2024 blog post says "American Foreign Archaeological Research"; AFAR's own
 site [Secondary] says "Academic". ▶ The 2026 blog post (live) also says "Academic".
- **Who runs it [Official]:** the Director of Global Studies (also an Upper School history
 teacher), who founded and leads AFAR.
- **AFAR structure [Secondary]:** a separate 501(c)(3) "based in Davidson, North Carolina";
 "incorporated as a 501(c)3 non-profit in 2007" after a first Belize season in 2006
 (https://www.goafar.org/history).
- **When it started:** credential "since 2021" [Official]. AFAR dates from 2006, before the
 director joined Davidson Day (Charlotte Magazine [Secondary]: moved here in 2010). The
 school does not publish when Davidson Day first sent students on AFAR.
 ▶ The school's own archived International Research page does: "Since inception in 2006",
 and the archived program page says the director "has been at Davidson Day School since
 2010".
- **Across divisions:** travel in Middle and Upper School only; no Lower School or Early
 Childhood travel structure published.

sections.text:
- **Name and start [Official]:** "This Diploma Distinction has existed at Davidson Day
 School since 2021". Page created 2026-03-06, published 2026-03-18 per metadata.
- **Grades:** Upper School; Research Methods in grade 11, Capstone in grade 12.
- **Current requirements [Official]:**
 - Core Course: "Honors Anthropology"
 - Elective Courses, "Choose Four": "AP World History or AP European History", "AP
 Environmental Science", "AP Psychology", "AP Macroeconomics", "AP with WE Service
 Recognition", "AP Spanish Language & Culture or AP French Language & Culture"
 - Language Competency Requirement: "Completion of Level IV or 3 levels of the same
 language in Upper School."
 - Practicum: "At least 100 hours of an approved internship, volunteer opportunity, or
 pre-collegiate program"; "Quarterly Ethics Labs"
 - Scholars Research Program: "Research Methods Honors Course (11th Grade)"; "Capstone
 Research Honors Mentorship (12th Grade)"
 - Culminating Diploma Experience: "Seniors present their capstone research project at the
 Davidson Day Scholars Research Conference."
- **Conflict — travel requirement [Official vs Official]:** the older program page: "The
 research component of the program requires a minimum of two weeks of international field
 research, either through Davidson Day School's AFAR Program or another approved
 international research project… Travel experiences without a scientific core, mission
 experiences, and study abroad will not fulfill this requirement." The 2026 Distinction
 page lists no mandatory travel: "Practicum experiences—often including international
 travel, research initiatives, language immersion, or cross-cultural service—become the
 foundation". Reported, not resolved.
- **Conflict — language requirement:** older page snippet "a minimum of four levels in the
 same language" vs. new "Completion of Level IV or 3 levels of the same language in Upper
 School." ▶ Verified on the Wayback copies of the older page: "A world language class each
 year with a minimum of four levels in the same language. Alternatively, the requirement
 can be met by completing the AP level of one world language."
- **Beyond the requirements [Official]:** "participation in special programming, such as a
 lecture and workshop series, epicurean tastings, and travel experiences", plus academic
 conferences. Forward-looking: "As the Global Studies pathway matures, students will have
 additional opportunities to participate in international service trips, language
 immersion programs, or find their own international opportunities".
- **Graduate counts:** NOT PUBLISHED; the only figure is the "nine" Diploma students among
 ten Calgary presenters in fall 2024. **Award:** NOT PUBLISHED.

- **Conferences [Official]:** Mount Royal University Archaeology Conference, Calgary, fall

 A Maya-themed conference at Disney's Coronado Springs Resort, Florida, "hosted by AFAR";

▶ The archived International Research page names the conference "the University of
Calgary's annual archaeology conference"; every later school page says Mount Royal
University. It also names a virtual "Maya at the Playa Conference", and says AFAR "hosts
two international conferences each year". The Nov 2025 Wayback copy of the program page
adds "Friedberg, North Carolina, for excavations" to that year's list.

 (published 2026-10-05); see §3 notes.

 signature program"; students apply "At the end of their sophomore year" to one of three

sections.text:
- Charlotte Country Day [Secondary, its own site]: an "Office of International Studies"
 with a named director and two coordinators; multiple Upper School trips with published
 dates; sister-school exchanges and Academic WorldQuest results.
- Providence Day [Secondary, its own site]: "Since 2007, more than 250 students have
 graduated with an additional diploma in Global Studies, the first in the nation"; its
 GSD FAQ site gives "2005 had the first graduating class of 5 GSD students. Since then
 more than 325 students have graduated with the diploma." (Conflict within PD's pages.)
- Charlotte Latin: no reliable comparison source.
- Interpretation: Davidson Day's offering is narrower and more specialized (field
 archaeology rather than a multi-destination travel office) and publishes far less
 logistical detail.

sections.text:
1. Earliest grade for each trip — the Middle School Spain/France trip, and AFAR Spain,
 Belize and Portugal for Davidson Day students?
2. What trips run in 2026–27 and summer 2027? Is the Middle School Spain/France trip
 running in 2027, and when?
3. Middle School trip cost, deposit schedule, inclusions?
4. Does need-based aid (Clarity) cover trips? What does the "$500 - $1,000" Field
 Experience fee pay for?
5. A travel fund, endowment or school scholarship beyond AFAR's 20% maximum?

# Davidson Day School — International Travel — Source URLs

fetched with `curl` (browser user agent) and its text read; pages gone from the live site
were read from the Wayback Machine, located through the CDX index. It checks the
AI-generated `Davidson Day - International Travel - Deep Research.md` against live pages.
That deep-research file is a lead sheet; **this file is the citation record.** A fact
reaches the app only if a row here verifies it (or `/implement` adds a row after verifying
it itself).

**Verification levels**
- **fetched** — page text retrieved 2026-10-18 and the claim read in it.
- **Wayback** — gone from the live page; present in the named snapshot.
- **PDF only** — in the deep-research PDF, not yet checked against a page. **Not sufficient
 to render.** `/implement` fetches it, or drops the claim.
- **404** — the URL no longer resolves.
- **third-party** — fetched, but from a site other than the school's. Renders only under
 the event/network exception and the user's decision recorded in the plan.
